## Highlights

- Strengthened release reliability with verified native libcurl setup, Rust 1.85-compatible queue accounting, and current Android SDK tooling.
- Removed actionable CI deprecation warnings across Windows packaging and Android build workflows, and prevented macOS Qt deployment warnings from unused SQL plugins.

## Fixes and Maintenance

- Kept atomic queue-slot accounting compatible with the declared Rust 1.85 minimum by using a compare-exchange loop.
- Built and verified the native libcurl dependency in Rust compatibility CI instead of exercising an unconfigured system fallback.
- Replaced deprecated Android SDK Manager invocations with the current Android SDK command-line interface.
- Updated the Android external-link icon to its RTL-aware AutoMirrored Compose variant.
- Resolved Visual Studio runtime discovery during Qt deployment and excluded unused SQL driver plugins from macOS packaging; a source guard prevents this exclusion if Qt SQL becomes a native dependency.
- Replaced Windows CI package-manager and artifact-download steps that emitted deprecated Node.js subprocess and Buffer warnings.

## Validation

- Passed the strict code and security quality gate, Rust compatibility and full verification, Android shared-core/JVM/APK validation, and CodeQL analysis for Rust, Java/Kotlin, JavaScript/TypeScript, and GitHub Actions.
- Built the native desktop application for Windows x64/ARM64, Linux x64/ARM64, and macOS Intel/Apple silicon.
- Passed Windows x64 and ARM64 installer compilation, installation, and uninstall smoke checks.
- The macOS bundle keeps required platform and QML plugins while excluding unused SQL drivers before Qt deployment.

## Alpha Scope

This is an alpha preview. Cross-platform feature parity and live-device acceptance remain in progress. The signed automatic updater remains disabled until its production endpoint and verification key are configured. Stable production releases continue to require complete parity coverage.
